thread:
marc: Customer reported rerank returning scores that don't match candidate order, and sometimes API throws 422. Repro on our side with TS SDK 0.19.3.
marc: Steps: call /v1/rerank with body from TS SDK bulk helper (batch of 3 candidates). Server responds 422 or returns scores in different order than candidates.
marc: Example payload we received from client (sanitized):
```json
{
  "query": "Which article is best?",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "text": "A"},
    {"id": "c2", "text": "B"},
    {"id": "c3", "text": "C"}
  ]
}
```
marc: What actually hit the server (from request log):
```json
{
  "query": "Which article is best?",
  "candidates": {"0": {"text": "A"}, "1": {"text": "B"}, "2": {"text": "C"}}
}
```
marc: Notice candidates became an object with numeric keys (not an array). TS SDK seems to accidentally convert arrays to objects when building payload for batch rerank.
jess: Do we know what code path causes it? Maybe JSON.stringify on a Map or using reduce? any stack traces?
simon: I grabbed the SDK bundle — the helper does `Object.fromEntries(candidates.map((c,i)=>[i, c]))` in the batch path. Looks like a bug introduced in 0.19.2 that tried to preserve indices for sparse arrays.
simon: That explains the server 422 since our validator expects an array. When we do accept it, the ranks get misaligned because server sorts by candidate index but code interprets numeric keys differently.
dana: Can you paste the request-id and example server error?
marc: request_id: r-0b7f3aa2, server log snippet: `422 score_count_mismatch: candidates 3 vs scores 3 but indices mismatch`. Full log: `ERR r-0b7f3aa2 rerank: invalid_candidate_shape \"expected array\"`
marc: Minimal repro (TS):
```ts
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference-js';
const r = new Redwood({ key: process.env.RW_KEY });
await r.rerank.batch([ { query: 'Which article?', candidates: ['A','B','C'] } ]);
```
This produces network payload with numeric keys.
jess: Thanks. Short-term mitigation: ask customers to pin SDK to 0.19.1 or use Python SDK. I'll draft a support reply asking for SDK version and temporaries.
simon: I'll open an internal bug. Patch idea: change the batch builder to ensure `candidates` stays an array and add a test for JSON shape. PR will target 0.19.x and patch 0.19.4.
dana: Can you attach a minimal repro repo/gist? Customer wants a quick workaround.
marc: Gist link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/mock-rerank-bug (private) — includes failing payload and curl fallback.
eng-runtime-oncall: We saw 4 similar incidents in logs over past 24h, all same request_id pattern. Good catch, escalate to eng-runtime for hotfix.
simon: I'll draft PR now, cc eng-release. If urgent we can publish hotfix and a patch release.
support-bot: Ticket INC-12345 created and linked to customer case 6521.
marc: Reply to customer: "Thanks — we identified a bug in TS SDK 0.19.2/0.19.3 that may change candidate array shape for batch rerank. Workaround: downgrade to 0.19.1 or submit payload as explicit curl (array). We're preparing a patch and will update you when 0.19.4 with fix is released." :thumbsup:
jess: I'll own comms, mark as high-priority, and send note to the customer with workaround and ETA.
dana: Adding acceptance test to SDK and also integration test on server to return 400 for object-shaped candidates (instead of trying to accept and misalign). Better to fail fast.
simon: Agreed. I'll attach unit test and release notes.
marc: Customer replied: "Thanks — workaround worked, will wait for patch." Closing loop for now.
marc: Filed internal follow-up (ENG-8732) to add more validations and a telemetry metric for malformed rerank payloads.
